name: Isolani-free open centre

plans.label: Central outpost
plans.description: With no pawn tension to calculate, piece placement is the game: plant a knight on a central square an own pawn still guards.

success.note: A White knight occupies d5 or e5 as a Tabiya-detected outpost.

plans.label: Seize the open file
plans.description: Double the heavy pieces on the open central file before it can be neutralized, and convert the file into an entry square.

success.note: File ownership is a piece-placement contest with no single square to test.

plans.label: Central outpost
plans.description: The same contest from the other side: a knight on a guarded central square outweighs a nominally freer bishop.

success.note: A Black knight occupies d4 or e4 as a Tabiya-detected outpost.

plans.label: Neutralize the file
plans.description: Challenge the open file with a rook, trade the heavy pieces on it, and steer toward the level ending symmetry promises.

success.note: Neutralization is measured in trades and time, not in one position's arithmetic.

watch: Whose rooks reach the open central file first.
Whether any central outpost square survives for a knight.
The wing pawn majorities that decide the ending once the pieces come off.
typicalMistakes: Conceding the open file while planning to challenge it later.
Posting a bishop where a knight belongs and vice versa.
Trading into a wing-majority ending without counting whose majority runs faster.

sources: UNGROUNDED: agent-authored strategic claims with no citation, engine evaluation, corpus frequency, or owner review; open-centre doctrine rendered from model knowledge.

Trigger narrowing: 'open centre' here means at least one fully pawnless central file with both queens still on (queens distinguish this family from the symmetrical-queenless entry) and no IQP catalogue match ('isolani-free'). Centres that are open in the practical sense but keep one mobile pawn per side on the central files do not fire; the vocabulary has no notion of pawn tension or mobility.
